subject: Gigawell Dedicated sizing: model scaling, KV-cache and quantization playbook
messages:
From: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@gigawell.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Vanessa — thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering lead asked that I share expected workload patterns so we can size the Dedicated pool. High level:
- 3 production endpoints (inference, chat-assist, embedding-indexing)
- Typical concurrent sessions: 120 steady, spikes to ~380 during batch runs
- Target P99 latency: <300ms for chat-assist (response start)
- Average input length: 1.2k tokens; peak sessions will hit 64k tokens for long-document retrieval with KV-cache used aggressively

Two specific asks:
1) For a model variant (open-llm/longformer-70b equivalent) with 64k context and heavy KV-cache retention, what GPU class and per-GPU slot sizing do you recommend?
2) If we use 4-bit quantization vs fp16, what are the practical memory and perf tradeoffs we should expect for both steady and spike scenarios?

I've attached a quick usage CSV (will upload sizing sheet later). Can we set up a 30-min workshop tomorrow to walk through numbers?

— Miguel
Miguel Santos, CTO
GigaWell Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Miguel — great context, thanks. I've looped in Aditya (inference engineering) and Laura (solutions) so we can convert this into a concrete Dedicated sizing proposal. Initial notes:
- 64k context with persistent KV-cache per session is the dominant memory factor; model parameters + activation + KV roughly determine the per-slot resident memory.
- For long-context workloads we typically recommend H100 80GB or A100 80GB class GPUs for the base pool; if you plan to rely heavily on 4-bit quant to save memory, we still need headroom for KV activations and batching.

Action items:
1) Aditya — can you produce a quick per-session memory breakdown matrix (fp16, int8/4-bit) for a 70B-type architecture at 1k / 8k / 64k context?
2) Laura — I'll share sizing sheet; please propose a reserved pool + burst policy (min guaranteed slots, burst to on-demand) and an ops runbook for cache eviction.

Miguel — booking 30 min for 2027-05-10 10:00 PT; invite to follow.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Miguel / Vanessa — attached is the quick memory matrix we discussed (attached as gigawell_sizing_v1.xlsx in the Drive link). Summary highlights from profiling a 70B-ish transformer variant with Redwood runtime primitives: (numbers are approximate, per active session)

- fp16 (no KV cached): model params + activations ~ 68GB; with conservative batching headroom plan 80GB slot
- fp16 + persistent KV-cache (8k context): +~6–8GB depending on tokenizer tokenization patterns
- fp16 + persistent KV-cache (64k context): +~42–48GB; total ~110–116GB -> requires multi-slot sharding (e.g., 2x 80GB GPUs per session with KV offload)

- 4-bit quant (GGUF-style quant or Redwood int4 path): model params memory drops ~2.8–3.2x; a 70B goes to ~22–25GB for params, activations still dominate during decode but some runtime kernels are quant-friendly
- int4 + 64k KV-cache: KV footprint unchanged (KV stores key/value activations), so persistent KV remains the primary memory driver; expect total resident memory per session ~70–78GB (params+activations+KV) depending on attention cache layout

Operational implications:
- If you rely on 4-bit quant, single 80GB GPU slots can host more sessions by param memory savings, but KV-cache retention at 64k pushes many sessions over single-GPU capacity. Plan for KV-sharding or multi-GPU session footprints or offloading to host/GPU peer memory.
- Batching: steady concurrency can be efficiently served with continuous batching; spikes require reserved burst slots to maintain P99 SLOs.

I'll bring a short set of per-slot configuration examples to the workshop.

— Aditya (Inference Eng.)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Miguel — following up with proposed Dedicated layout and ops guardrails. High-level proposal:

1) Reserved pool (Guaranteed):
   - 12 x H100-80GB slots (for baseline throughput of chat and embedding peak steady-state)
   - Each slot configured for multi-session tenancy: target ~8–10 concurrent short-to-mid sessions at fp16 or ~16–20 at int4 for non-64k sessions

2) KV-heavy sessions (64k context):
   - Treat these as "large sessions" with dedicated multi-GPU footprints (recommended: 2x80GB GPUs per large session)
   - Implement automatic routing policy: tag requests with KV-expected-length and route to large-session pool or fallback to reduced context with summarization when large capacity exhausted

3) Burst capacity:
   - On-demand autoscale up to +18 GPUs (H100/A100 mix) with pre-warmed instances for predictable cold-starts

4) Eviction and cache policy:
   - Time-based TTL for KV (e.g., 12–24h depending on usage) with LRU for session prioritization
   - Prefer prefix caching (retain only recent KVs for long-running sessions) unless request explicitly requires full 64k context

5) Cost note: using int4 reduces committed GPU count by ~30–40% for non-64k sessions but yields marginal gains for 64k sessions because KV dominates. We'll include cost delta in the detailed sheet.

Next step: Marcus and Aditya to provide per-GPU costed scenario (reserved vs burst) and we can convert to an ARR estimate for the deal.

— Laura Bennett, Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Miguel — attached is quant_tradeoffs_20270509.pdf (summary) and kv_cache_profile.png (heatmap of KV usage across sessions). Key operational notes from infra perspective:
- If you commit to Reserved pool (12x H100-80GB), expected baseline sustained throughput meets your steady 120 concurrent sessions with P99 headroom at fp16.
- For 64k KV sessions we recommend enforcing a multi-GPU tenancy model; we can automate placement so that a large session is pinned across 2 GPUs and the runtime manages KV alignment.
- Offload options: NVMe-backed KV staging gives ~30–40% effective reduction in GPU DRAM pressure but adds tail-latency risk for read-heavy retrievals. Use only for non-latency-critical batch jobs (embedding-indexing).
- Suggested reserve+burst cost model included in the Drive sheet: shows breakeven point if GigaWell runs >2.2M tokens/day.

I also added a brief checklist for the pilot run: profiling artifact collection, tokenization sanity checks, and an ops runbook for degraded quant fallbacks.

— Marcus Lin, Infra

From: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@gigawell.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question + expected context length

Team — this is very helpful, thank you. A few quick follow-ups after reviewing the attachments:
- We're comfortable with multi-GPU large sessions. Can Redwood provide the runtime placement policy (doc link) so our infra team can mirror it in our VPC?
- For the NVMe offload option, please call out the expected P95/P99 latency delta in the doc so we can decide which workloads it is safe for.
- Can you seed the Drive folder with a sample profiling run for our tokenizer (we use SentencePiece) so we can validate the 64k token estimates?

We'll sign the pilot reserved commitment once the final cost delta spreadsheet is in place. Looking forward to the workshop notes.

— Miguel
